correctness.rationale: For fixed prime ell, multiplicativity yields nu_ell(sigma(n))=sum_{p^e||n}nu_ell(sigma(p^e)). For e=1, local term nu_ell(p+1). For e>=2, 0<=nu_ell(sigma(p^e))<=(e+1)log(p)/log(ell) and nu_ell(p+1)<=log(p+1)/log(ell), so |difference|<=C_ell e log p; averaging over n<=x bounds the error by C_ell sum_p sum_{e>=2} e log p / p^e<infinity, hence error/loglog n converges to 0 in density. For each fixed J, g_{ell,J}(n)=sum_{p|n}min(nu_ell(p+1),J) is strongly additive; min= sum_{j<=J}1_{p=-1 mod ell^j}. Each fixed reduced progression has reciprocal prime sum (1/phi(ell^j))loglog x+O(1); Turan-Kubilius variance is O_{ell,J}(loglog x), implying density concentration at c_{ell,J}loglog n. For j>J, mean of nonnegative tail is bounded by sum_{j>J}sum_{p<=x,p=-1 mod ell^j}1/p. Uniform Brun-Titchmarsh for ell^j<=x^delta gives O_{ell,delta}(ell^{-J}loglog x); for larger ell^j elementary harmonic counting of p=k*ell^j-1 gives O(log x * x^{-delta})=o(1); Markov then J->infinity. Sum_{j>=1}1/phi(ell^j)=ell/(ell-1)^2, including ell=2 with coefficient 2. n with n<=x^a has density 0 for any fixed 0<a<1, justifying loglog n versus loglog x. This reconstructs the proof, not merely finite tests. Local inequality and all quantifiers verified for fixed ell only. value.rationale: The fixed-prime exponent of the natural multiplicative sum-of-divisors function is a motivated arithmetic statistic. The exact typical coefficient ell/(ell-1)^2 quantifies density-one prime-adic divisibility, distinguishes ell=2 from odd primes and relates it to the hierarchical arithmetic progressions p=-1 mod ell^j. This is more than a known local table and supplies an independently useful leading constant; no downstream general theorem or paper-scale requirement is imposed. Standard proof tools and the possibility of earlier general coverage limit claims of scope but do not alone negate the mathematical utility. It does not claim an exceptional-set rate, fluctuations, or uniformity in ell.
